nodes.title: Titus: Grace That Trains
nodes.summary: Titus is left in Crete — whose own poet called Cretans 'liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons' — to appoint elders and build a culture of good works on a foundation of pure grace: 'the grace of God has appeared… training us to renounce ungodliness,' and 'he saved us, not because of works done by us in righteousness, but according to his own mercy.'

prerequisites.reason: Titus condenses 1 Timothy's church-order manual for a rougher mission field; the letters pair.

nodes.discussion_prompt: Paul says the same grace that saves people also trains them to renounce ungodliness. How can kindness change a person's behavior in ways that rules alone cannot, and where have you seen that happen?
assessment_questions: Why did Paul leave Titus in Crete, and what did he tell him to do there?
Titus 3 says God saved us according to his own mercy, and a few verses later insists believers devote themselves to good works. How does the letter hold mercy and good works together?
Paul wants Christians in a culture famous for lying and laziness to be known for good works. What good work could make the gospel visible where you live, and what stops you from starting it?

teaching_concepts.explanation: Elders are judged by proven lives and faithful doctrine rather than charm, because false teaching corrupts whole households.
The grace that brings salvation also teaches believers to renounce ungodliness and live self-controlled, godly lives now.
Rescue comes from God's kindness and the Spirit's renewing work, never from works we perform to earn it.
Mercy received turns into visible good works, so the lives of believers adorn the teaching about God in public.

nodes.completion_criteria: Explain how Titus holds together salvation by God's mercy and a life devoted to good works.

comprehension_check.question: Titus is told to build churches out of people famous for lying and laziness. Where does the letter say the changed life comes from?
options: From rules firm enough to restrain old habits
From godly training that earns saving grace
From leaders strict enough to model the standard
From the same grace that brought the salvation
comprehension_check.why: Titus 2:11-12 gives grace the teacher's chair: what appeared bringing salvation now trains believers out of the old life.
comprehension_check.hint: Read Titus 2:11-12 again. Notice what grace does after it brings salvation.

comprehension_check.question: Titus 2:10 gives ordinary working people a surprising power over the church's message. What can their conduct do?
options: Make the teaching about God credible to watching outsiders
Repay a portion of the mercy God has shown
Complete the salvation that mercy only began in them
Shield the young churches from imperial suspicion
comprehension_check.why: Titus 2:10 lets honest daily work put the teaching about God on public display at its most attractive.
comprehension_check.hint: Read Titus 2:9-10 again. Notice where the verse says the effect of honest work finally lands.
